description:
Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) and Alternative Provision (AP) Adviser

As a general requirement the Supplier will:

provide valuable expertise to advise, challenge and support at risk or poor performing local areas/local area partnerships in continuing to develop and implement robust and achievable plans to improve its SEND and AP services.

provide advice and support to ensure the pace of improvement is appropriate and that improvements to the SEND and AP system are sustainable;

ensure plans remain focused on outcomes for children and young people with SEND and inform the quality of the service in readiness for the next Ofsted inspection.

provide support and advice as necessary when assessing and driving progress, taking account of the weaknesses identified by Ofsted and of other diagnostic work (including DfE Vulnerable Children's Unit (VCU) assessments);

apply expertise and experience to support the local area/local area partnership's senior leadership and SEND management team in addressing areas of weakness; this will include working with practitioners of different levels to develop competence and improve performance, and help foster a culture of reflection, challenge and support.

make use of wider partners to support and advise the local area/local area partnership on potential solutions to issues and signpost examples of good practice where possible;

engage at both strategic and operational level

contribute to the department's formal reviews of the local area/local area partnership's progress and make a recommendation to VCU on whether progress has been sufficient;

provide regular written reports to the department on the local area/local area partnership's progress to VCU, and more frequently if the pace of progress is not sufficient.

have an awareness of the proposed SEND/AP system and Children's Social Care reforms including the Change Programme and work closely with relevant colleagues in supporting and challenging local areas/local area partnerships.

develop working relationships with Health partners where this helps achieve the objectives set out in the contract.

If the local authorities named in this agreement are part of the Delivering Better Value or Safety Valve programmes, the supplier must liaise with any Advisors working with the local authority on those programmes to ensure coherence and consistency of approach. These meetings / contacts should be undertaken as part of the days allocated in this contract.

title: T23/0112Culture Connect Data Observatory
description:
The Arts & Humanities Research Council (AHRC) Creative Communities programme is a £1.5 million UK Research & Innovation (UKRI) investment that aims to capture new understanding of how culture can address regional inequality and help level up the UK. We are working with academic, third and private sector partners to identify and profile examples of good practice and innovations in partnership working and to explore the potential for AHRC research to help build creative communities of the future across all nations of the UK.
    Our audiences include policy makers and government audiences of all scales, third sector workers, communities, academics and researchers, and others.
    We are inviting bids to co-develop and pilot a new open access data observatory for culture in the North of Tyne Combined Authority (NoTCA); the biggest geographic devolved area in England from May 2024. The pilot will bring communities, cultural organisations and venues, the devolved authority (as well as its 12 member councils) and national government closer together to better understand the cultural footprint of public users as they move across the cultural offerings of the devolved region. It aims to upskill users to achieve a new awareness and agency of their data and digital footprint through an integrated cross-sector approach to sustainable digital literacy and co-creation within a city region.
    The project has been co-designed with national (DCMS, ACE, RSA) and devolved partners (M10, WYCA, NoTCA, Newcastle Cultural Compact and NGCV, Newcastle City Council) to ensure it is fit for purpose and can achieve maximum reach and impact within the timeframe of funding.
    Developing a shared, live database, the pilot will enable new exchange of knowledge between stakeholders interested in using data for social good. Public users will be acknowledged and rewarded for their engagement through enhanced user experiences from the participating cultural organisations and venues, while the cultural sector and devolved authorities will benefit from access to new data and insight about how, where and when community members move across cultural spaces within a place. The collaborative governance of the pilot will produce an ongoing dialogue as the website is developed and piloted so that it is co-evaluated from inception and generates long-term relationships that can be adopted by the parties and taken forward beyond the lifetime of the award.

title: GB-Newcastle upon Tyne: InfoBlox Universal DDI (UDDI) Solution, 23/01/26 - 22/01/29
description:
Northumbria University is seeking to appoint a single supplier under the JISC Network Solutions framework (Lot 7 - InfoBlox).  The contract term will be 36 months.
      
      We are seeking to procure a comprehensive solution to support our network services infrastructure through the deployment of Infoblox technology.  This procurement is intended to enhance the management, visibility and resilience of our DNS, DHCP and IPAM (DDI) services, while ensuring robust reporting capabilities and long-term support.
      
      The scope of this tender covers the acquisition of Infoblox Universal DDI (UDDI) solution including software tokens, hardware, professional deployment services, training and a three-year maintenance support agreement.  The proposed solution will enable scalable management of DDI services across our environment, with a focus on operational efficiency, security and compliance.
      
      Key Technical Requirements:
      
      •Replacement of current Infoblox DHCP infrastructure - Replace two existing Infoblox 1415 HA physical appliances with one physical appliance and one VM appliance configured in HA pair, located in our Colo Data Centre. UDDI DHCP to be configured in HA mode.
      •Configuration of UDDI portal for Single Sign On (SSO), to enable role-based access. 
      •Reporting capability - Reporting functionality within UDDI for the DHCP element of the solution.
      •NIOS Grid integration - Integration with existing NIOS Grid to support Read/Write configuration capability, enabling support for remaining DNS/IPAM objects.
      •Professional services - Professional services to support migration from NIOS DHCP to UDDI DHCP solution before the following key milestone dates: 
      a.1st February 2026 - End of licensing for current DDI DHCP solution
      b.April 2026 - End of support for current 1415 DDI appliances
      
      The bill of materials includes:
      
      •Management Tokens: 4 units of IB-TOKENS-UDDIMGMT-1000 to support centralised DDI management.
      •Server Tokens: 3 units of IB-TOKENS-UDDI-SERV-500 to enable DDI services across designated server infrastructure.
      •Physical Server: 1 unit to host the Infoblox services and ensure high availability.
      •Reporting Tokens: 25 packs of Infoblox Reporting Token Pack (40 tokens / year) to support detailed analytics and reporting over the contract term.
      •Deployment Services: professional services to ensure successful implementation, configuration and knowledge transfer.
      •Training: 3 Infoblox Education Instructor-led Training and On-Demand Annual Subscription User License.
      •3 year Maintenance Support: to ensure continuity of service and rapid resolution of any hardware or software issues.

title: GB-Newcastle upon Tyne: T23/0114 - Ellison A - E - Category C Remedial Works
description: NOTE: This notice was updated on 07 October 2024 for the following reason: Original contract value was £222,831.00. This value has increased to £316,928.98 due to the following. At the start of the current phase of works, the contractor surveyed the Ellison facades and undertook hammer testing to the green tiles and vertical concrete sections. A number of cracked tiles and loose tiles were identified with the proposed method of repair to be an epoxy resin injection in and behind the tiles to ensure adhesion to the masonry behind.  Following agreement on the repair method, the contractor has removed several of the green tiles to Ellison C & D on the quad side.  It then became apparent the ease of removal as well as the original form of construction being a basic 'dot & dob' of concrete with a c.1" void between the tile and the masonry.  This has subsequently ruled out this repair method and has raised additional H&S concerns regarding the adhesion of the tiles throughout the Ellison Blocks and the subsequent risk of the dot & dab failing, particularly where moisture has been entering the structure .  Our Structural Engineers (Fairhurst) have advised that until a longer-term re-cladding scheme for the blocks is implemented, that we maintain existing exclusion zones and that we install fall arrest netting to the tiled bays throughout the north facing elevation of Ellison D.  Furthermore, amendment allows for the the urgent make safe at weekend due to the urgent H&S nature of this, and price for the netting as a variation under the existing JCT contract as well as additional work identified further. Finally it has been noted that the latchway mansafe fall protection systems is missing. The mansafe system is needed to carry out the netting works and requires a new latchway and training for T Manners to complete the work.(There was a sudden façade defect on Ellison Building A in the summer of 2023. The area was immediately made safe and scaffolding and catchment netting erected. Shortly thereafter, structural surveys were instructed. The outcome was a list of recommendations for remedial repairs, and the defects were categorised under various risk levels depending on the severity and level of risk. The works for this contract are defined as Category C Remedial Works and Surveys on Ellison A - E buildings.)

title: MFDs
description:
1.	BACKGROUND 

Bishop Bewick Catholic Education Trust 

1.3.1	Bishop Bewick Catholic Education Trust was established in 2020 and has grown rapidly to its current size of 39 schools across Newcastle upon Tyne, North Tyneside & Northumberland. Our mission is to ensure that all children in our schools experience the best education possible. Part of this mission is to ensure that our partnerships with contractors support the best possible outcomes for our pupils and staff and offer good value for money in a consistent manner across all our school sites.

1.3.2	Our Vision - Together, we are greater than the sum of our parts.
1.3.3	Our Mission - A great education has the power to transform lives through:
1.3.4	Opportunity - to provide excellent education for our children and to be drivers for social justice in our schools.
1.3.5	Love - everyone feels parts of the wider Trust, not just their individual school
1.3.6	Collaboration - By harnessing the strengths we have collectively, we have so much more capacity to support and improve the education of all children within Bishop Bewick
1.3.7	Development - everyone is valued and cared for as if one family
1.3.8	Aspiration - we believe each individual is unique and has their own purpose in life


2.	OBJECTIVE

2.1	This FC sets out the requirements of this procurement and provides information on how the tender process will be managed. It also explains the clarification process and confirms the process that will be used to evaluate Tender(s). 

2.2	Bishop Bewick CET aims to deliver the following objectives through this procurement:
•	Improved use of technological solutions to deliver an efficient and convenient service for end users
•	Improved printing speeds and quality 
•	Achieving best value for money
•	Changing printing cultures to reduce waste and improve energy efficiency measures 




2.3	This Further Competition is for Wave 1 which includes 18 schools who have initial requirements. These schools have at least one contract due to expire prior to 31st August 2026. Details on the schools, the number of devices and monthly print volumes can be found in Appendix G1.

2.4	The Trust is seeking to enter overall a 45-month contract with a co-terminus end date of 31st August 2028. Each leasing agreement will be entered into as part of this overall contract and will have co-terminus end date of 31st August 2028. 

2.5	The Trust are looking to appoint a Supplier who will demonstrate technical competency and best value for money in relation to the Trust's requirements, as well as a focus on sustainability. 

2.6	The Trust are planning on a further procurement process in 2026 to review the remaining 20 schools within a procurement for Wave 2. The list of schools in Wave 2 is provided in Appendix G2.

2.7	The tender is for a third-party provider to provide the provision of MFD's for the following schools within BBCET.
